papers.title: Constraining deviations from the Teukolsky equation with GW250114
papers.abstract: The recent gravitational-wave detection GW250114 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) Collaboration provides unprecedented precision for testing general relativity (GR) through black hole ringdowns. In this study, we provide the first bounds on theory-agnostic deviations from the Teukolsky equation as described by the beyond-Teukolsky formalism. It directly connects deviations in the perturbation equations on the level of the effective potential in the Teukolsky equation with changes in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum. We incorporate information on the final mass and spin from a full LVK inspiral-merger-ringdown analysis as parametrized priors in our analysis, reflecting theoretical uncertainties. Using publicly available LVK posterior information on agnostic damped sinusoid parameters, we then demonstrate how much beyond-Teukolsky potentials can be constrained. The high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) allows us to avoid the expensive full Bayesian analysis of all parameters and to work directly with a simplified likelihood for the fundamental QNM only. This strategy is promising for future events with even higher SNR and allows, in principle, for a quick and simple test of theories beyond GR without performing the full data analysis procedure. We report that current bounds on deviation parameters are in agreement with the Teukolsky equation.

ai_review.summary: This paper uses GW250114 ringdown measurements to constrain phenomenological modifications of the Teukolsky effective potential. It maps potential-deformation coefficients into changes of the fundamental quasinormal frequency and combines published damped-sinusoid posteriors with mass and spin information from an inspiral–merger–ringdown analysis. A Gaussian likelihood approximation makes the calculation inexpensive. Two prior prescriptions widen the remnant-parameter uncertainty to represent possible departures from the general-relativistic prediction. When varied individually, the tested complex deformation coefficients remain consistent with zero. The contribution is a practical translation from spectral measurements to perturbation-equation parameters. The resulting bounds depend on that prior construction, the single-mode approximation and the treatment of theoretical uncertainty, so they are best viewed as conditional constraints motivating a fuller joint analysis.

ai_review.quality_reason: The inspected analysis defines an explicit likelihood and explores alternative remnant priors using public posteriors. The constraints remain sensitive to simplified uncertainty handling and one-at-a-time deformations rather than a full joint waveform analysis.

Only the fundamental mode and individually varied deformations are used. Dependence on GR-informed remnant posteriors and omitted sky-localization uncertainty limit the interpretation. papers.title: Popcorn EMRIs: Transient Gravitational Wave Signals and Their Analysis in Schwartz Space
papers.abstract: This study investigates extreme-mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) with orbital periods exceeding the observation windows of mHz gravitational wave detectors. During their early, highly eccentric stages, these systems produce periodic gravitational wave eruptions at pericentre, separated by long quiescent periods. We define these systems as ``popcorn EMRIs''--bound, coherent binaries in a deterministic evolutionary phase. This distinguishes them from stochastic, non-coherent bursts associated with parabolic fly-bys. Using a steady-state model based on the phase-space continuity equation, we estimate the population within a Milky Way-like galaxy. Because these estimates depend on sensitive astrophysical variables like stellar relaxation and density profiles, our figures are illustrative rather than absolute. For a one-year observation baseline, we estimate a steady-state population of 200 to 2,000 popcorn EMRIs, significantly outnumbering the 10 to 88 continuously observable EMRIs. This yields an expected rate of 5 to 44 detectable eruptions per year. Despite high signal-to-noise ratios (exceeding 700 for Galactic Centre events), the low duty cycle confirms their transient nature. Standard data processing techniques, designed for continuous signals, often employ windowing that distorts eruption morphology and artificially reduces the signal-to-noise ratio. To address this, we establish a mathematical apparatus using based on standard smoothing techniques, in the theory of tempered distributions. We demonstrate that standard windowing techniques irreversibly degrade the signal-to-noise ratio of transient sources when the taper overlaps the eruption, and we utilize Schwartz space regularization to justify the direct Fourier transform as the energy-preserving estimator.

ai_review.summary: This paper considers highly eccentric, bound EMRIs whose orbital periods exceed a detector's observation window, producing isolated pericenter eruptions. An analytic steady-state continuity model estimates their Galactic-center population and rate, while a LISA noise prescription supplies illustrative signal-to-noise values. Under the adopted two-mass population model, the authors predict hundreds to thousands of long-period systems and several to tens of observable eruptions per year. They also use Schwartz-space smoothing to discuss transient Fourier analysis and attenuation when a time-domain taper overlaps an eruption. The contribution connects an early EMRI population to a specific signal-processing issue. Its numerical rates remain model-dependent, and the formal energy-preservation argument requires care when translated into optimal inference with realistic colored noise and finite data.

papers.title: QPEs from Warped Disk Collisions with EMRIs: Brightness-Recurrence Diagram and Gravitational-Wave Follow-up
papers.abstract: Quasi-Periodic Eruptions (QPEs) display correlated long/short and strong/weak patterns that remain unexplained by existing flat-disk collision models. We propose that these features arise from an extreme-mass-ratio inspiral (EMRI) colliding with a warped accretion disk, likely formed after a tidal disruption event. The warp modulates both recurrence time and burst energy, encoding the disk geometry -- and thus the spin of the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) -- into the X-ray light curve. We introduce the Brightness-Recurrence Diagram (BRD) to visualize this correlation, where QPE bursts trace an elliptical trajectory driven by the EMRI's apsidal precession; the tilt of this ellipse encodes whether the EMRI is prograde or retrograde relative to the SMBH spin. Applying this model to the prototypical QPE source GSN 069 successfully reproduces the observed patterns. The data are consistent with either a prograde stellar secondary or a retrograde stellar-mass black hole. In the stellar-mass black hole scenario, ongoing orbital decay could render the EMRI detectable by LISA within a few decades, facilitating gravitational-wave follow-up and independent multimessenger constraints on the system.

ai_review.summary: This paper proposes that collisions between an EMRI and a warped accretion disk explain correlated brightness and recurrence intervals in quasi-periodic X-ray eruptions. A brightness–recurrence diagram organizes the predicted pattern into an elliptical track driven by orbital precession, whose orientation depends on orbital direction and secondary type. Applied to GSN 069, the model accommodates either a prograde star or a retrograde stellar-mass black hole. Simplified post-Newtonian trajectories and Gaussian flares roughly reproduce selected light-curve epochs, although the secular decline in flare amplitude is missed. The contribution is a geometric diagnostic linking disk structure, EMRI motion and electromagnetic observations. A future LISA signal could help distinguish interpretations, but that prospect depends on the black-hole-secondary scenario and uncertain long-term disk-driven evolution.

papers.title: Polarization of strongly lensed gravitational waves as a probe of the lens-induced orientations of electromagnetic counterparts
papers.abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a well-established phenomenon in electromagnetic (EM) observations, where the lensed images and arcs are resolved on the two-dimensional sky and constrain the mass distribution of the lens. Strongly lensed gravitational waves (GWs) are also expected to be detected routinely by next-generation detectors, but their multiple images are recorded only as one-dimensional time series without positions. Among them, lensed binary neutron star mergers can be accompanied by EM counterparts with resolvable structures, such as relativistic jets. In EM lensing, the lens-induced change in the apparent orientation of such a structure can be measured only relative to other images or statistically, because its intrinsic orientation is not directly observable. In this work, we show that the GW polarization, which the lens leaves unchanged, provides this missing reference, i.e., a compass, so that the orientation offset of each image can be measured in absolute terms. We place this orientation layer on the EM image plane together with image positions from the lensed host arcs and Fermat-potential heights from GW time delays and magnifications. Using a mock population of such mergers observable by the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer, we find that the predicted image positions and arrival times are calibrated once the detection selection is included. The lens-induced orientation offsets reach tens of degrees and are detectable in up to a third of the events, at viewing angles above about $40^\circ$ for quadrupole-dominated signals.

ai_review.summary: This paper proposes using gravitational-wave polarization as a reference for the intrinsic orientation of a resolved electromagnetic counterpart in a strongly lensed merger. Comparing that reference with each apparent jet axis measures an image's lens-induced orientation offset. The framework combines these offsets with image positions, delays and magnifications, then forecasts performance with mock binary-neutron-star populations and a joint Fisher analysis. Under favorable assumptions, orientation offsets are measurable in up to about one third of selected events. The contribution is an additional local lens diagnostic that is invariant under a mass-sheet transformation. Practical opportunities are restricted because polarization is best measured at inclinations where jets are harder to observe, and real jet–orbit misalignment and counterpart uncertainties reduce the forecast yield.

papers.title: Lense-Thirring induced repeating blast trains in continuous gravitational waves
papers.abstract: We characterise gravitational lensing induced by the Lense-Thirring effect in a continuous gravitational-wave source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. This scenario is very likely to generate lensing events, as long as the source's orbital inclination is not aligned with the black hole's spin axis and the Lense-Thirring timescale is shorter than the observational window. The signal appears as short-duration ($T_{\rm blast}$) gravitational-wave "blasts" that repeat after every orbit ($T_{\rm orb}$) within a limited time window ($T_{\rm train}$). The blasts' signal strength depends on the system's geometry and not on the black hole mass. The signal will go silent and renew twice in a full Lense-Thirring precession period.

ai_review.summary: This paper analyzes repeated lensing of continuous gravitational waves from a source orbiting a spinning supermassive black hole. Lense–Thirring precession periodically brings the orbit close to edge-on, producing a train of short amplified episodes at successive conjunctions. The authors derive orbital, precession, blast and train timescales and examine an illustrative neutron star around Sagittarius A*. Large peak magnification is offset by a small duty cycle, so the integrated detection gain is modest. Detecting the recurring pattern requires an orbital model that preserves coherence despite rapid Doppler modulation. The contribution is a distinctive lensing timing signature tied to frame dragging. Its observational prospects depend on a rare close neutron-star system, its spin and ellipticity, and sufficiently accurate orbital tracking.

papers.title: SPLIT: Loosely-coherent inference of long-inspiral gravitational-wave sources for robustness against modeling and data outliers
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will detect gravitational waves (GWs) from dozens of extreme- and intermediate-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs/IMRIs). These sources will stay in-band for months to years, offering extraordinary scientific potential. However, their fully phase-coherent analysis standard in current pipelines imposes stringent waveform accuracy requirements; failing to model the signal over such long durations can result in significant systematic biases. To address this, we formulate a robust Bayesian inference framework that segments the data into blocks, infers each block coherently, and recombines the results using loosely-coherent phase information. By restricting full phase-tracking to much shorter block durations, this approach prevents significant accumulation of phase errors. We implement this methodology in \textsc{SPLIT} (Segmented Posteriors for Long-Inspiral Templates), a GPU-accelerated Python package. Applying \textsc{SPLIT} to an environment-rich injection, we demonstrate that while a fully-coherent vacuum-GR analysis incurs a maximum 1D systematic bias of $\approx 4.8σ$ from the truth, the shorter integration window of our loosely-coherent approach restricts such biases to $\lesssim 0.5σ$. Overall, despite a fractional loss of optimal signal-to-noise ratio, the substantial improvement in parameter accuracy offered by our method presents a highly advantageous trade-off for LISA and other future GW detectors.

ai_review.summary: SPLIT introduces a loosely coherent Bayesian framework for long EMRI and IMRI signals whose phase evolution may be modeled imperfectly. It analyzes shorter coherent blocks with a heavy-tailed likelihood and connects their evolving parameters through a flexible Markovian prior. A GPU implementation uses sequential Gibbs sampling. Vacuum injections agree with coherent baselines, while an accretion-perturbed IMRI example reduces the largest reported parameter bias from about 4.8 to 0.5 standard deviations with five blocks. The contribution is a tunable robustness–precision trade-off for inference before more accurate coherent follow-up. Its enlarged posterior space is costly to sample, and the demonstrated improvement depends on a limited injection set and chosen hyperparameters rather than a comprehensive realistic-LISA validation.

papers.title: Degeneracies in the quasinormal mode spectrum of the Kerr-Sen black hole
papers.abstract: The non-Hermitian nature of the eigenvalue problem underlying black hole perturbations can induce the presence of exceptional points (EPs) in the quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum. EPs are points in parameter space where QNMs become degenerate. Near an EP, QNMs are resonantly excited, leaving imprints on the ringdown signal. In this work, we investigate the exceptional structure of scalar perturbations of the Kerr-Sen black hole, a rotating, charged solution of the low-energy limit of heterotic string theory, and compare it with the EP structure of the Kerr-Newman black hole in General Relativity. Starting from the EP associated with a massive scalar field in the Kerr limit, we trace exceptional lines in the parameter space spanned by the black hole spin, charge, and field mass. We locate these degeneracies directly by imposing double-root conditions on the QNM secular equation, thus avoiding the need for parameter space scans. We also investigate the hysteresis phenomenon, showing that encircling an EP in parameter space leads to an exchange of the associated QNMs.
authors: Sérgio V. M. C. B. Xavier

ai_review.summary: This paper studies exceptional points where two scalar quasinormal modes of a Kerr-Sen black hole coalesce, and compares their structure with Kerr-Newman. Instead of scanning the spectrum across parameter space, the authors solve a continued-fraction secular equation together with its frequency derivative, tracing degeneracy lines in spin, charge and scalar mass. The lines remain near extremality and reach the massless-scalar plane; following modes around an endpoint exchanges their labels. A nonrotating WKB comparison and a near-extremal asymptotic expansion provide consistency checks. The contribution is an efficient way to map spectral topology and identify path-dependent mode assignments. Its implications for observable gravitational ringdown remain prospective because the calculations concern test scalar fields rather than coupled gravitational perturbations.

papers.title: Eccentricity detectability in Extreme Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) consist of a stellar-mass compact object orbiting a massive black hole and are among the primary targets for the future space-based gravitational-wave detector LISA. Their orbital eccentricity carries valuable information about their astrophysical origins, making its detection particularly important. However, increasing eccentricity has competing effects on detectability: it makes eccentric waveforms easier to distinguish from circular ones, but also redistributes signal power across multiple harmonics, reducing the power captured by single-harmonic searches. In this work, we quantify this trade-off within a semi-coherent framework for a source with fixed total SNR of $50$. Eccentricity becomes distinguishable from zero for final eccentricities $e_f \gtrsim 0.05$, while single-harmonic sensitivity declines beyond $e_f \simeq 0.1$. In noise-free analyses, including enough harmonics to recover at least $50\%$ of the total SNR avoids this degradation, but adds statistical freedom when calibrating detection thresholds. We apply the framework to two astrophysical EMRI populations, showing how these competing effects interact with their eccentricity distributions under simplified assumptions. The balance among eccentricity-driven distinguishability, harmonic power loss, and the statistical cost of additional harmonics is an important consideration for future EMRI search developments.

ai_review.summary: This study asks when LISA can identify nonzero eccentricity in an EMRI using a computationally cheaper semi-coherent search. FastEMRIWaveforms injections compare eccentric and circular hypotheses, first without noise and then with detector response and calibrated noise thresholds. At fixed total matched-filter SNR 50, eccentricity becomes distinguishable around final eccentricity 0.05, but a single harmonic loses sensitivity above roughly 0.1 as power spreads across harmonics. Multiple harmonics mitigate that loss in noise-free tests; their noisy detection benefit remains uncalibrated. Controlled relaxation and Hills populations illustrate different detectability patterns. These results clarify an important search-design trade-off, but their fixed Schwarzschild systems, orientations and tightly restricted eccentricity-search parameters prevent interpretation as realistic population rates or blind-search forecasts.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes and tidal responses of black holes in generic anisotropic matter environments
papers.abstract: We develop a perturbative framework for a black hole embedded in a generic, possibly anisotropic, matter environment under spherical symmetry. Our approach extends previous analyses restricted to vanishing radial pressure or to perturbative matter configurations. Within this framework, we derive an analytical generalization of the Einstein cluster that incorporates a polytropic radial pressure, and we investigate the properties of this solution. We show that both the geodesic structure and the axial quasinormal-mode spectrum remain predominantly governed by an overall gravitational redshift effect, while the radial pressure systematically enhances the environmental corrections. In contrast, the tidal Love numbers are substantially more sensitive, and can exhibit order-unity deviations, including vanishing and negative strictly static magnetic Love numbers for sufficiently large anisotropy. We present the full linearized equations, which can be applied to various extensions, including ringdown analysis and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals.

ai_review.summary: The authors extend relativistic perturbation theory for a spherical black hole surrounded by anisotropic matter with nonzero radial pressure. A polytropic generalization of the Einstein cluster supplies analytic backgrounds, while strictly static and irrotational prescriptions close the axial perturbation equations. Geodesic and axial quasinormal-mode corrections are dominated by an environmental redshift enhanced by radial pressure, with sixth-order WKB results supporting the leading analytic scaling. Magnetic tidal Love numbers respond more strongly in relative terms and can change sign under one prescription, although their normalization and interpretation require care. The framework helps organize environmental effects relevant to ringdown and future inspiral modeling. It remains an effective-fluid model with inner-region energy-condition violations, closure dependence and no completed polar-sector phenomenology.

papers.title: Quasi-Normal Modes and thermalization in integrable Quantum Field Theories from the Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz
papers.abstract: We propose a Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) approach for describing thermalization in integrable quantum field theories. The exponential damping and oscillations when approaching thermal equilibrium can be understood as the analogs of quasi-normal mode (QNM) frequencies of black hole perturbations within the framework of holography. Holographic intuitions and some general properties of thermal Green's functions motivate the existence of such a TBA formulation, as well as lead to the imposition of a nonstandard analytical structure on the QNM TBA, while comparison with integrable form-factor expansions fixes the remaining ingredients. We conjecture the QNM TBA to be equivalent to performing an all-order resummation of secular terms in a thermal form factor expansion of retarded 2-point correlation functions. We compare the predictions with tensor network simulations of the E8 deformation of Ising CFT at nonzero temperature. We conjecture that the QNM TBA framework should also be applicable for describing out-of-equilibrium approach to Generalized Hydrodynamics (GHD).

Holographic relations between thermal correlators and black-hole quasinormal modes motivate an unusual analytic continuation, while selected secular terms in form-factor expansions determine driving terms. The construction reproduces an exact Ising damping result and the leading low-temperature expansion. For the interacting E8 theory, predicted complex frequencies enter a fit to tensor-network simulations, with eleven complex amplitudes adjusted. This offers a potentially efficient route around difficult real-time resummations, but all-order equivalence, the full mode spectrum and generalized-hydrodynamic extensions remain conjectural. Its connection to the digest is primarily conceptual: these thermal-field-theory modes do not directly supply astrophysical black-hole ringdown or EMRI predictions.

papers.title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
papers.abstract: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

papers.title: Implementation of a five-wave approximate Riemann solver for general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics in AthenaK
papers.abstract: We present an implementation of an HLLD approximate Riemann solver for the AthenaK astrophysics code with support for full general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics via a tetrad frame transformation. Our implementation uses an initial guess for the HLLD iterative solve which eliminates the need for an additional conserved-to-primitive inversion, which greatly accelerates performance without affecting accuracy. Additionally, by coupling the method with a first-order flux correction, we are able to use the method reliably even when the magnetization exceeds $10^4$, which we achieve in a SANE accretion disk. Our SANE disk shows that HLLD leads to a more strongly magnetized funnel and more accurate horizon fluxes when compared with HLLE. We further apply the new HLLD implementation to an equal-mass binary neutron star merger. For our long-lived remnant, HLLD enhances the magnetic shear stresses in the outer layers and leads to weaker differential rotation. However, due to weaker gravitational wave emissions in the post-merger phase, the remnant is consistently less compact while producing more dynamical ejecta and a more massive disk. The cost of this new solver is relatively modest thanks to the improved initial guess: our accretion disk tests are only ${\sim}10-25\%$ slower than HLLE, and for our binary neutron star runs with a microphysical equation of state, we find that HLLD is only ${\sim}3\%$ slower than HLLE across all runs.

papers.title: Response of Circular Binaries to Monochromatic Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: The exchange in specific orbital energy between a test particle in a Keplerian binary orbit and a continuously incident linearized gravitational wave (GW) is considered. Analytical expressions for the rate of change of energy, semi-major axis and mean motion of the test particle are derived. Numerical solutions illustrate a resonance effect betwen the GWs frequency and the particle's initial orbital frequency. We distinguish between bounded short-period oscillations and resonant libration. The effect of the GWs angle of incidence with the particle's orbital plane is also considered. Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.

papers.title: Probing parity-breaking black-hole geometry with extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational-wave signatures of equatorial reflection symmetry breaking in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) around a parity-violating conformal Kerr black hole. For the circular-orbit branch connected to equatorial Kerr orbits, we derive the dynamics through second order in the dimensionless deformation parameter $\varepsilon$ and construct adiabatic inspirals and gravitational-wave signals using a mass-quadrupole prescription. Equatorial reflection maps $\varepsilon$ to $-\varepsilon$, making the polar displacement odd and the orbital frequency and energy even in the deformation. The induced first harmonic has a small direct contribution for the configurations studied, while second-order dynamical corrections accumulate over many cycles to produce appreciable dephasing. We find that rapid black-hole rotation enhances these phase effects and the associated noise-weighted waveform mismatch. For a one-year inspiral of a $10M_\odot$ object into a $10^6M_\odot$ black hole with $a/M=0.9$ and viewing inclination $ι=2π/3$, the fixed-parameter mismatch reaches the comparison benchmark $\mathcal M=0.01$ at approximately $\varepsilon=10^{-3}$, without optimization over time, phase, or Kerr parameters. A single-parameter Fisher analysis also indicates improved local sensitivity to $\varepsilon$ at high spin. These results connect the reflection properties of the circular branch to accumulated source-phase effects and complement tests of propagation birefringence.

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.

papers.title: Impact on Inferred Neutron Star Equation of State due to Nonlinear Hydrodynamics, Background Spin, and Relativity
papers.abstract: Tidal interaction is a unique, detectable signature in gravitational wave signals from inspiraling binary neutron stars (BNSs), which can be used to constrain the neutron star (NS) equation of state (EoS). The tidal interaction is resonantly amplified as the orbital frequency approaches the NS fundamental mode (f-mode) frequency. It has been shown that the exclusion of tidal resonance in parameter estimation leads to a significant bias in the inferred NS tidal deformability and hence the NS EoS [Pratten et al. PRL 129, 081102 (2022)]. The strength and location of tidal resonance depend sensitively on the f-mode frequency, which is typically modeled using its universal relation with the tidal deformability that is derived for an isolated, non-spinning NS assuming only linear fluid perturbations. In a BNS inspiral, the f-mode frequency can be corrected by at least three known effects: nonlinear hydrodynamics, background spin, and relativity. We use Hamiltonian Monte Carlo simulations to estimate the systematic bias on tidal deformability when each frequency correction is ignored. Our study considers both loud, individual events and the stacking of a population of detections. Both scenarios are expected when the next-generation detectors are available with a sensitivity level increased by about an order of magnitude.

papers.title: Eccentricity greatly enhances the detectability of line-of-sight acceleration in gravitational wave signals
papers.abstract: Compact object binaries formed dynamically are characterized by a tail of eccentric sources and by the potential presence of environmental perturbations. Here we show that the presence of eccentricity in a gravitational-wave (GW) signal strongly enhances the sensitivity to environmental effects, focusing in particular on line-of-sight acceleration (LSA). We demonstrate that this enhancement is recovered in Fisher-analysis forecasts and, crucially, persists in full Bayesian parameter estimation using state-of-the-art eccentric waveform models. The key insight is that the signal should be analyzed from the moment the first detectable eccentric harmonic enters the detector band, rather than from the customary entry of the $n=2$ harmonic: this allows to probe the early inspiral and thus a longer signal, over which the GW dephasing introduced by LSA becomes substantially larger. We show that with this approach constraints on LSA can increase by more than an order of magnitude between eccentricities at 20~Hz $e_{20}=0$ and $e_{20}\sim0.1$, for signals with sufficient signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR), while we predict a factor $5$ amplification even for low-SNR ones. Fully exploiting this effect necessitates the continued improvement of efficient eccentric waveform models and likelihood evaluations, enabling the efficient analysis of signals lasting thousands of seconds and containing a large number of harmonics.

papers.title: Shaping black hole resonances II: Spectroscopic landscapes and interference in black hole ringdown
papers.abstract: We map analytically the excitation of Schwarzschild quasinormal modes (QNMs) $C_n$ by oscillatory Gaussian perturbations across the pulse width $σ$ and carrier frequency $ν$. The excitation coefficient of each mode is determined by the product of an intrinsic excitation factor and a source-dependent overlap evaluated at the complex QNM frequency. For oscillatory Gaussian perturbations, this overlap is the coherent sum of the positive- and negative-frequency branches of the source, with its amplitude factorizing exactly into a Gaussian spectral envelope and an interference factor. We observe that the excitation amplitude peaks at $ν=ω_n^{\rm Re}$ only for narrowband sources. For sufficiently broadband pulses, the maximum lies at $ν=0$, so efficient excitation does not necessarily require matching the carrier and the mode frequency. We observe that the interference between branches, modulates the amplitude only for nonzero $ν$, a feature generic to real oscillatory sources. The prominence of the interference-induced modulation is controlled by the ratio $ω_n^{\rm Re}/ω_n^{\rm Im}$. The phase separates into a mode-only, a width-only and a $ν$-dependent term, the last generated by the same interference, with $ν=0$ being its unique maximum at fixed width. The analytical predictions are validated against time-domain numerical simulations, showing a relative median error of $\sim 4\%$ for $|C_0|$. For $|C_1|$, the median error is $\sim 16\%$ when $σ\leq 5$, increasing to $\sim 36\%$ across the full parameter space. The median phase difference for $n=0$ is $\sim0.14 \,\rm rad $ and for $n=1$, $σ\leq5$ it is $0.34\,\rm rad$. Our results demonstrate that QNM excitation cannot be understood through frequency matching alone and may provide qualitative insights into more realistic astrophysical scenarios.

papers.title: Chaotic motion of spinning particles in nonlocal gravity
papers.abstract: We study spin-induced chaos around a static, spherically symmetric black hole in revised Deser--Woodard nonlocal gravity (NLG), using the conservative test-body approximation relevant to extreme-mass-ratio inspirals. The deformation parameter $ζ$ describes departures from Schwarzschild spacetime. Poincaré sections, rotation curves, and fast Lyapunov indicators (FLIs) reveal changes in resonant structures and a decreasing fraction of non-plunging trajectories classified as chaotic within the sampled family, from $37.5\%$ at $ζ=0$ to zero at $ζ=0.1$. The FLI classifications of selected trajectories are reflected in their approximate mass-quadrupole waveforms: neighboring chaotic and regular trajectories show a marked local spectral-flatness contrast, which weakens in backgrounds where both are classified as regular. To assess whether a transition from chaotic to regular motion caused by the background deformation helps distinguish NLG from GR, we compare NLG waveforms at $ζ=10^{-6}$ with GR waveforms generated at different initial radii. For a trajectory whose classification changes between the backgrounds, this adjustment substantially reduces the mismatch. The selected NLG waveforms from chaotic orbits retain larger minimum mismatches than those from regular orbits, although sensitivity to initial conditions may also hinder signal recovery. These results connect background-dependent orbital dynamics with radiation spectra, but do not establish that chaos offers an advantage for identifying the background geometry.

papers.title: Cosmography with gravitational waves II: Padé approximants in an extended redshift regime
papers.abstract: We evaluate the capability of next-generation gravitational-wave detectors, including LISA, the Einstein Telescope, and DECIGO, to probe cosmographic parameters using electromagnetically bright standard sirens. Adopting Padé approximants, we extend the cosmographic analysis to substantially higher redshifts and constrain the parameters $H_0$, $q_0$, $j_0$, $s_0$, and $l_0$. We examine the constraints primarily as a function of the number of detections and, in a complementary analysis, across correlated SNR--redshift regimes. LISA provides percent-level constraints on $H_0$, while the Einstein Telescope and DECIGO reach subpercent precision as the catalogue size increases. The parameter $q_0$ can be constrained at the tens-of-percent level, whereas the higher-order parameters $j_0$, $s_0$, and $l_0$ remain progressively less determined. Compared with the low-redshift Taylor analysis, the Padé approach extends the usable redshift range, increases the accessible event population and enables a higher-order reconstruction of the expansion history.

papers.title: Kerr metric perturbations in Lorenz gauge via numerical relativity methods
papers.abstract: Gravitational self-force calculations are needed to accurately describe the motion of a small body in a spinning (Kerr) black hole spacetime, which is vital to predict gravitational wave signals from asymmetric-mass compact binaries. Accurate calculations for the upcoming LISA mission require a minimum of second perturbative order in the mass ratio, which has thus far only been achieved for nonspinning (Schwarzschild) black holes due to nonlinear complexities of the Einstein equations. In this work, we calculate Kerr metric perturbations with a new computational approach based on numerical relativity methods, extending recent scalar self-force results to full general relativity. We formulate the perturbative Lorenz-gauge Einstein equations in terms of azimuthal $m$-modes in the frequency domain and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using a spectral discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and preconditioned iterative solvers. With our new method, we achieve exponentially convergent first-order gravitational self-force calculations for circular equatorial orbits in Kerr spacetime up to spin $|a|/M=0.998$ (the Thorne limit). Our framework is designed to carry over to second order by delivering accurate and well-behaved first-order data for nonlinear source construction, and as a solver for the second-order metric perturbations themselves.

papers.title: Probing (sub-)solar-mass black holes and superspinars with current and next-generation gravitational-wave observatories
papers.abstract: We investigate the detectability and parameter estimation prospects of (sub-)solar-mass collapsed binaries with current and next-generation gravitational wave detectors, allowing the dimensionless component spins to extend phenomenologically beyond the Kerr bound, $(|χ|>1$) (where $χ$ is the spin parameter). Using the inspiral-only TaylorF2 waveform and a Fisher-matrix analysis, we study binaries with component masses in the range $0.1\!-\!2\,M_\odot$ and compare the performance of Advanced LIGO with that of a third-generation network consisting of Cosmic Explorer and the Einstein Telescope. We find that third-generation detectors substantially improve the signal-to-noise ratio and the measurement of intrinsic binary parameters, particularly the component spins, while also providing significantly improved sky localization. For favorable configurations, the primary spin can be measured with precision $Δχ_{1z}\sim10^{-3}-10^{-2}$, demonstrating enhanced sensitivity to potential Kerr-bound violations. However, strong anti-correlations between the component spins limit the interpretation of small marginalized spin uncertainties as definitive evidence for superspinars. We also examine formation scenarios for (sub-)solar-mass collapsed binaries and show that dense dark-matter environments, particularly the Galactic Centre, can significantly enhance their formation and merger rates. Our results demonstrate the potential of future gravitational wave observations to probe low-mass collapsed objects and possible departures from the Kerr bound, while highlighting the need for physically consistent superspinar waveform models and Bayesian model comparison for a definitive interpretation.

papers.title: Bardeen spacetime as quantum corrected black hole: Grey-body factors and quasinormal modes of gravitational perturbations
papers.abstract: We study axial gravitational perturbations of the asymptotically flat Bardeen spacetime interpreted as a string-T-duality-inspired quantum-corrected Schwarzschild black hole. Starting from the anisotropic-fluid background, we derive the Regge--Wheeler-type master equation and the corresponding effective potential, and compute quasinormal modes with high-order WKB--Padé and time-domain methods. We show that increasing the quantum-correction scale $\ell_0$ raises and shifts the barrier inward, causing the black hole to ring at higher frequencies and decay more slowly. The same deformation suppresses low-frequency transmission, shifts the onset of grey-body factors to larger frequencies, and reorganizes the partial and total absorption cross-sections. Overall, the results identify a clear and consistent imprint of short-distance regularization on both ringdown and scattering observables.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes of dyonic axion black holes with nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study quasinormal modes (QNMs) of static charged black holes with a massless axion and nonlinear electrodynamics (NED). Without NED corrections, we compute the complex QNM frequencies of five oscillatory mode families in the system of five dynamical degrees of freedom. These families are continued from the fundamental Reissner--Nordström (RN) modes. Axion coupling generically breaks gravitational and electromagnetic parity isospectrality. At representative nonzero couplings, all five frequencies are distinct even on purely electric RN backgrounds without axion hair. Adding magnetic charge sources axion hair, couples all five perturbations, and modifies their oscillation frequencies and damping rates. Additional purely imaginary growing modes occur in some strong-coupling benchmarks. The known electromagnetic--scalar spectral degeneracy at $Q/M=\sqrt{7}/4$ for $\ell=2$ in the decoupled RN limit explains the linear frequency splitting induced by a small axion coupling. We include two quartic NED interactions obtained by squaring the two standard electromagnetic invariants. With the axion decoupled and equal quartic coefficients, electromagnetic duality makes the first-order NED frequency shift of each individual gravitational or electromagnetic branch independent of electric--magnetic charge composition at fixed $Q/M$. For unequal coefficients, duality instead constrains the sum of the first-order NED frequency shifts within each isolated RN parity pair. Depending on the coefficients, NED increases or decreases the damping rates by about one percent in representative backgrounds, while the quartic terms remain small compared with the local Maxwell energy density throughout the exterior. The QNM frequencies and NED shifts obtained with the spectral method agree with independent integration-and-matching results at representative parameter values.

papers.title: The inclination cross-check: binary-pulsar timing and gravitational-wave polarimetry
papers.abstract: Radio timing and gravitational-wave (GW) polarimetry provide independent measurements of a binary's inclination. We study their consistency through $\eps=s_{\rm Shapiro}-s_{\rm GW}$, where $s_{\rm Shapiro}$ is the Shapiro-delay shape and $s_{\rm GW}$ is inferred from the tensor polarization amplitudes. We combine a time-dependent, finite-arm detector response with radio timing averaged over each integration, retaining the amplitude--inclination covariance and the nonlinear orientation posteriors. For hypothetical 15-minute binaries at 5 kpc and $65^\circ$ inclination, four years of GW data and a 125-h radio campaign give $σ_\eps=5.4\times10^{-3}$ for a double neutron star and $1.0\times10^{-3}$ for a pulsar--black-hole binary when two static timing harmonics are fitted. An apsidally evolving radio model with $e=0.01$ and a free apsidal rate gives $4.5\times10^{-3}$ and $0.94\times10^{-3}$, respectively, with the circular GW covariance held fixed. Changes in the relative tensor amplitudes can be absorbed by the GW fit as an apparent inclination shift and revealed by the radio measurement. An inaccurate detector response can produce a similar discrepancy even when its Fisher errors are nearly unchanged. These forecasts use the $n=2$ GW harmonic and assume a fixed orbital plane, sustained radio visibility, and the specified timing precision; additional harmonics can provide further orientation information.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes, complex null geodesics and singularity resolution in regular AdS black holes
papers.abstract: The black hole singularity is hidden behind its horizon, and it is difficult to determine whether it is resolved by quantum gravity or stringy effects. For an AdS-Schwarzschild black hole, it is known that the two-point function of the dual conformal field theory has a singularity associated with a null geodesic that bounces off the black hole singularity. In this paper, we investigate how the resolution of the black hole singularity is encoded in the dual conformal field theory by considering regular AdS black holes as regularized geometries. Using WKB analysis, we compute the quasinormal modes of regular AdS black holes and read off the dual two-point functions from the modes. We find that the singularity corresponding to the bouncing null geodesic for singular black holes is replaced by a smooth bump associated with a complex, rather than real, null geodesic. The location of the complex geodesic singularity is supported by analyzing the structure of the operator product expansion for the two-point function. Our results provide a holographic signature of black hole singularity resolution and clarify how information about the regular interior is encoded in boundary correlation functions.

papers.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). AstroVink-TREX: Automated strong gravitational lens segmentation as input for mass modelling pipelines
papers.abstract: Strong gravitational lens modelling requires the lens light, lensed source light, and contaminants to be separated in each image before mass modelling codes can fit the system. Within Euclid this separation has so far been done by hand, which does not scale to the more than 15,000 candidates in the Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) catalogue of Data Release 1 (DR1). We present AstroVink-TREX , a neural network that performs this separation automatically and predicts three flux maps, in a standard format directly usable by mass-modelling pipelines. The network uses a hybrid architecture, pairing a vision transformer encoder reused from the lens detection network with a parallel convolutional branch. A custom loss function penalises both flux and structural error, while allowing independent weighting per component. From the network's predictions we also derive the modelling centre, fitting region, conjugate points, and binary maps, providing all the inputs that a modelling pipeline needs to run without manual setup. We evaluate the efficiency of the network on DR1 systems against existing fits and through expert validation. Across approximately 3000 inspected systems, taking 75% agreement between inspectors, just 39 lens models fail because of a segmentation error. Following this validation, the network provides the component separation and modelling setup for every system modelled in DR1. With automated segmentation, lens modelling is no longer limited by manual preprocessing and can now operate at the same scale as lens discovery.

papers.title: Axial gravitational-wave propagation and mass--gravity identifiability in conformal scalar--tensor lensing
papers.abstract: We investigate tensor-wave propagation in a specified massless, unscreened conformal scalar--tensor theory using a static Einstein--scalar exterior matched to a weakly self-gravitating matter lens. The odd-parity gravitational master potential has a scalar-charge correction at radial order $R^{-4}$ for fixed Einstein-frame mass. Its next $R^{-5}$ coefficient depends on $\ell(\ell+1)-9$, reversing sign between the quadrupole and higher multipoles; we test the expansion against the exact exterior potential. We connect this result to the locally normalized post-Newtonian light-deflection parameter and distinguish the Schwarzschild baseline at fixed Einstein-frame mass from that at fixed measured matter mass. A finite-radius WKB expansion reveals cancellation of the leading frequency-dependent potential moment for the quadrupole at fixed multipole, whereas a separate fixed-impact-parameter limit recovers an achromatic geometrical-optics action and a subleading axial contribution. Independent null-geodesic bending and numerical quadrature check these limits. For a point lens, achromatic observables constrain an effective mass rather than the lens mass and scalar coupling separately. An illustrative two-image Fisher calculation quantifies differential-phase identifiability after arrival-time and constant-phase nuisance parameters are released. The phenomenological phase experiment is separated from action-derived propagation quantities; model-specific dispersive observations require a complete matched image transfer function.

papers.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
papers.abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced $s$-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.

papers.title: Multimessenger Exoplanets: Combining Infrared Excess and Astrometry with Gravitational-wave Detections of Double White Dwarf Exoplanets
papers.abstract: Multimessenger astrophysics provides a powerful framework for characterizing astrophysical systems through multiple, independent signals rather than relying solely on electromagnetic (EM) observations. While most prior multimessenger studies have focused on the properties of ultracompact objects, recent work has shown that gravitational waves (GWs) detectable with the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) observatory can also be used to detect exoplanets orbiting stellar remnants. In particular, this includes circumbinary planets around tight double white dwarf (DWD) systems. This population is unique: no such planets are currently known around DWDs, and only a handful of circumbinary planets around main-sequence stars and planets orbiting white dwarfs (WDs) have been identified. Independent EM confirmation will be essential, especially for the first GW-detected exoplanets, to validate this method. While EM techniques are unlikely to efficiently survey large populations of DWDs, GW detection followed by targeted EM confirmation provides one pathway for identifying and characterizing these systems. Using a representative case, the known DWD ZTF J2243+5242 scaled to a fiducial distance of 150 pc, we compute the detectability of circumbinary exoplanets via LISA GW observations. We then demonstrate two complementary EM techniques--JWST infrared (IR) excess and Gaia or Habitable Worlds Observatory astrometry--that could independently confirm a GW-detected planet in this fiducial system. We present the first exploration of IR excess around DWDs as a viable exoplanet detection method, extending its established use for solitary WDs. Both EM techniques overlap with regions of parameter space where LISA is sensitive to DWD exoplanets, enabling robust confirmation and characterization.

papers.title: Receiving Exoplanet Messages with Gravitational-wave Carriers: The Gravitational-wave Radial Velocity Method
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) radial velocity (RV) may offer a new method for detecting exoplanets, one that would primarily target planets orbiting GW-emitting, ultracompact, post-main-sequence stellar objects such as white dwarfs, neutron stars, and black holes. In this work we show that while similar to electromagnetic-based RV, this GW-based method depends on the ''phase modulation index'' (PMI), a parameter that is more sensitive to high-mass, long-period exoplanets. We investigate the potential of GW RV for GW sources in both the mid-frequency spectrum (where the upcoming LISA mission will operate) and the high-frequency spectrum (where the current LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observatories operate). Remarkably, we find that the PMI increases by a factor of $\sim \mathrm{O}\left(10^4 - 10^6\right)$ going from the mid-frequency to the high-frequency GW spectrum, which results in a greater redistribution of observed power due to the exoplanet's presence. By analyzing the power content of the observed GW signal, we derive analytic expressions to predict the GW carrier frequency power loss due to the exoplanet and the signal-to-noise ratio of the GW source and the exoplanet. We also explore the effects of the additional Doppler effect caused by the motion of the GW observatory and the potential for GW source parameter bias introduced by the presence of an undetected exoplanet. All of this helps us better understand where the GW RV method may work best in the exoplanet mass-period discovery space.

papers.title: Multipoles in the IllustrisTNG simulation galaxies and implications for Strong Gravitational Lens modelling in Time-delay Cosmography
papers.abstract: Time-delay cosmography is a powerful independent probe of the Hubble constant ($H_0$), yet reaching the sub-2$\%$ precision required to resolve the Hubble tension demands a rigorous treatment of mass model systematics. We use realistic massive elliptical galaxies from the IllustrisTNG hydrodynamic simulation suite to characterise higher-order angular mass complexity in the form of multipoles ($m=1,3,4$) and quantify their impact on $H_0$ inference. We find that these multipole perturbations are common and emergent features of galaxy assembly; in 51$\%$ of our total samples ($54\%$ TNG100-1 galaxies and $85\%$ for TNG50-1 galaxies), the addition of multipole terms to a standard elliptical power-law model is preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion. Ignoring these structures in lens modelling introduces systematic biases in $H_0$: for perturbations of $\sim2\%$, the biases are of the order of 1--2$\%$ for $m=1$, 4--5$\%$ for $m=3$, and 3--6$\%$ for $m=4$ multipole. While the $m=4$ (boxy/discyness) mode induces a predictable directional bias, odd-order modes ($m=1,3$) introduce significant stochastic scatter. We demonstrate a degeneracy where unmodelled internal multipoles can be effectively absorbed by the external shear component. This combined with low signal-to-noise observations can create ``hidden biases'' where formally perfect fits to imaging data ($χ_ν^2 \approx 1$) could harbour significant cosmological errors. Our results provide an astrophysical basis for multipole priors and highlight the necessity of moving beyond rigid parametric models to achieve high-accuracy cosmography in the era of \textit{Euclid} and LSST.

papers.title: Gravitational-wave hierarchical inference from population samples
papers.abstract: Standard approaches to gravitational-wave population inference require evaluating the probability density of the population model. While appropriate for models composed of exact functional forms, this approach is not compatible with state-of-the-art astrophysical predictions from population-synthesis codes, which simulate samples from astrophysical models whose densities are unknown. We present an approach that solely requires samples and never density evaluations of the targeted population model. Key technical ingredients include efficient surrogates for the single-event likelihoods and detection probability, together with an efficient sampling strategy. Using detections up to GWTC-5.0, we validate the method against standard inference with a parametric model, showcase its flexibility on a simulated population including hierarchical mergers, and present a realistic application to a grid of astrophysical population-synthesis simulations with five formation channels. This work paves the way toward a direct comparison of astrophysical models and gravitational-wave data.

papers.title: The Gravitational Wave Foreground from Galactic Cataclysmic Variables in LISA
papers.abstract: Electromagnetic observations have been the primary medium for studying cataclysmic variable (CV) systems, capitalizing on the invaluable opportunity they present to study binary stellar evolution and accretion. The launch of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) mission, however, will enable a multi-messenger perspective of the population. We extend previous work to explore the gravitational wave (GW) spectra sourced by a local and Galactic population of CVs. Using the Bayesian LISA Inference Package (BLIP), we simulate LISA data containing these CV populations to understand their impact and our ability to jointly model CV and double white dwarf (DWD) GW spectra. While we find that a local CV population has negligible effect on the LISA datastream, a Galactic CV population will have a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 76, depending on the characteristics of the DWD population present, and will bias existing DWD spectral models if ignored. Current approaches struggle to accurately recover both populations' respective spectra, calling for the creation of multi-component spectral models that include GW contributions from both CVs and DWDs. These results point toward a promising future for the study of CVs with LISA.

papers.title: Effects of Lensing by Sgr A* on Semicoherent Searches for Continuous Gravitational Waves. I. Signal Model and Mismatch Studies
papers.abstract: Continuous gravitational waves (CWs) from neutron stars beyond the Galactic Center can be lensed by the supermassive black hole in Sgr A$^*$. Since the signal lasts far longer than the lensing time delay, the two geometric-optics images overlap and interfere. Transverse source motion during the observation makes their magnifications and relative time delay evolve, producing evolving amplitude and phase modulations absent from standard CW templates. Using lensed and unlensed injections in Gaussian noise, we quantify their effect on a Hough-based semicoherent search through a semicoherent mismatch. Recovery is governed by the competition between lensing amplification and waveform modulation. Smaller impact parameters generally improve recovery through stronger magnification, while higher transverse velocities partially offset this gain through faster modulation, especially at small impact parameters and short source-lens distances, where image interference is appreciable. The response also depends on the intrinsic signal strength. Loud signals exhibit small fractional changes, with net losses in some configurations, whereas weaker signals yield broader mismatch distributions extending to more negative values, indicating greater enhancement. A population study, sampling lensing parameters from astrophysically motivated velocity and source-lens distance distributions, reproduces the strong dependence on signal strength. Differences between populations are modest, but high-velocity, short source-lens distance populations tend towards larger mismatches. Lensing effects therefore cannot be accounted for by rescaling search sensitivity with the magnification alone; reinterpreting directed Galactic Center search sensitivities and upper limits under the lensing hypothesis requires injection studies with the full lensed waveform across the lensing parameter space.

papers.title: WDM_GW_Wavelets: A fast, JAX-based Python implementation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer wavelet transform for the time-frequency analysis of gravitational wave data
papers.abstract: This paper describes a JAX-based implementation of the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) time-frequency transformation, intended for use in gravitational-wave data analysis.

papers.title: Metric Reconstruction for Generic Black-Hole Perturbations
papers.abstract: Most sourced radiation-gauge reconstructions of Kerr perturbations use Hertz potentials. We establish the first self-contained Newman--Penrose transport hierarchy for reconstructing metric perturbations with generic conserved sources on Ricci-flat Petrov type D backgrounds. In a traceful radiation gauge, two first-order equations determine the trace, after which the total metric follows from an extreme Weyl scalar and the prescribed Ricci tensor without a Hertz potential. We illustrate the method for a Schwarzschild black hole with a thin static shell, including a source-supported static completion sector.

papers.title: Rapid Multiparameter Gravitational-Wave Tests of General Relativity with Neural Posterior Estimation
papers.abstract: Multiparameter gravitational-wave tests of general relativity (GR) are limited by strong correlations among post-Newtonian (PN) phase deformations and the computational cost of Bayesian inference. We present DINGO-TGR, a neural posterior estimation framework that jointly infers binary-source parameters and six PN phase deformations within the TIGER parametrization, using IMRPhenomXPHM waveforms with spin precession and higher-order modes. Importance sampling reweights the neural proposal samples, while principal component analysis (PCA) identifies two well-constrained combinations of PN deformations. We validate the framework using 16 zero-noise GR injections and 12 beyond-GR injections, recovering GR-consistent posteriors in the former and leading-mode shifts consistent with the injected deformations in the latter. For GW150914 and GW250114, our results agree with independent \texttt{bilby-tgr} analyses using \texttt{dynesty}. After training, inference including importance sampling takes approximately 38 minutes and 4.4 hours, respectively, compared with 177 and 238 hours for conventional sampling. GW150914 exhibits a mild offset from GR in the leading PCA mode, whereas GW250114 is consistent with GR. To assess the significance of the GW150914 offset, we analyze 1000 GW150914-like GR injections with independent Gaussian-noise realizations and fixed detector power spectral densities. The resulting empirical upper-tail $p$-value is $11.5\%$, indicating that the observed offset does not reject the adopted GR null model at the 5\% significance level. Our results demonstrate the potential of importance-sampling-corrected neural inference for efficient multiparameter GR tests and large-scale injection-based significance assessments.

papers.title: Localization of gravitational-wave source behind galaxy clusters by gravitational-wave lensing
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations have opened new opportunities to study massive object events like merging binary black holes. When combined with electromagnetic counterparts, accurate localization of gravitational-wave sources could allow us to identify their host galaxies and carry out follow-up studies, such as study the environment of merging black holes and determine the Hubble constant. One of the possible methods for precise localization is strong gravitational-wave lensing. Previous studies have considered strong gravitational-wave lensing with galaxy lenses. However, galaxy clusters have yet to be investigated due to the complexity of their mass structures. Here we take the list of known cluster lenses from the Hubble Frontier Fields, simulate lensing properties of gravitational waves from their reconstructions as they would be observed by the ground-based gravitational-wave detectors. When same model family is used in simulation and localization, we find that the correct lens is identified for around 90\% of the simulated events. We also show that the source positions within the cluster can be pinpointed at sub-arcsecond precision with an estimate on source redshift. When we marginalize over all possible lens models for the clusters, the lens identification and localizations remain valid as long as the correct lens model is contained in the available cluster lens models. However, most localization attempts fail at initialization if the correct cluster model is excluded. These tests establish a proof of concept of localization under idealized conditions, while more work is needed to understand the cluster lens modeling discrepancies and reconstruction bias to validate the approach further.

papers.title: Wave-Optics Imprints of Warm Dark Matter Subhalos with Prompt Cusps on Strongly Lensed Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Dark matter halos are expected to form with a prompt $ρ\propto r^{-3/2}$ density cusp at their centres, and in warm dark matter (WDM) cosmologies these cusps can dominate the inner structure of the low-mass subhalos that survive free-streaming suppression. We investigate whether that inner structure is visible to gravitational waves lensed in the wave-optics (WO) regime. Extending the strong lensing WO diffraction-integral framework to WDM, we generate subhalo populations with the {\sc sashimi-w} semi-analytic model, assign each subhalo a prompt cusp through a cusp-halo relation, and compute the frequency-dependent amplification factor $F(f)$ across the LISA band over 500 independent realisations for $m_χ\in \{6, 10, 20, 40, 80, 100\}$~keV. The signal is governed by the overlap between the WDM-suppressed subhalo mass function and the $m_{\rm sub} \sim 10^{4}$ to $10^{7}\,M_\odot$ range to which the LISA band is sensitive. Modulations are negligible for $m_χ\lesssim 10$~keV, reach the percent level by 40~keV, and then saturate to a CDM-like plateau, so the observable reliably probes $m_χ$ only over the intermediate range $\sim 20$ to 40~keV. Repeating the 40~keV ensemble on identical subhalo catalogs with the cusp amplitude set to zero, we find that prompt cusps enhance the amplitude modulation only mildly. Where cusps make up a large fraction of the subhalo mass, free-streaming has already depleted the signal-carrying mass range, and where that range is populated, the cusp lies well inside the Fresnel radius, to which the diffraction integral responds through projected enclosed mass rather than central density. A percent-level detection in a strongly lensed massive black-hole binary would therefore establish the presence of substructure on Fresnel scales without diagnosing its inner profile.

papers.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
papers.abstract: Magnetic fields can launch outflows through the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) or the Blandford-Payne (BP) mechanism in accreting black hole systems. Despite the dominant launching mechanism still being unclear, the BP process has been insufficiently studied in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations due to difficulties in generating and maintaining the required large-scale magnetic field geometry. Here, we set up six resistive GRMHD simulations of thin accretion disks with BHAC. The accretion disks in two simulations become magnetically arrested, while the others stay in the standard and normal evolution (SANE) regime. All simulations form jets and winds. The jets are parabolic and collimated by the outer sub-relativistic disk wind; a power law relating the jet width $x$ to the height $z$ as $x\propto z^\mathcal{K}$ yields exponents between 0.52 and 0.64. Among the SANE simulations, the setup with spin parameter $a_* = -0.9375$ has the strongest and most efficient jet, as it accumulates the most magnetic flux at the black hole horizon. For a highly spinning black hole with $a_*=0.9375$, the BZ jet power is $\gtrsim3$ times greater than the disk wind power. The simulated wind regions consist of a highly magnetized region, where the magnetization parameter $σ\gg1$, and a less magnetized region. A fast outflow with the potential to reach Lorentz factors up to $Γ_\infty\approx25$ propagates in the former region, but because the Lorentz force acts against the disk, it cannot remove a measurable amount of mass from the disk. In the less-magnetized region, a centrifugally driven slower wind efficiently carries away disk material.

papers.title: The Doppler effect of the Milky Way rotation on mHz gravitational waves
papers.abstract: We model the stellar density and the rotation curve of the Milky Way and compute the gravitational-wave spectrum of its unresolved binaries as a function of direction. Because the Galaxy rotates, the waves emitted along each line of sight are Doppler-shifted by a different amount, and we derive for the first time the resulting observed anisotropic spectrum, which no longer factorizes into a spectral shape times an angular template. We then quantify the observability of this distortion with space-based interferometers. With their nominal noise budgets, neither LISA nor a LISA+Taiji network can detect it: the residual between the models that include and neglect the rotation has a signal-to-noise ratio ${\rm SNR}_{\rm diff}\simeq0.2$ and $0.7$ after two years, and the induced bias on the foreground parameters stays below $0.1σ$. A tenfold better noise amplitude, of the order contemplated for post-LISA concepts, raises the residual to ${\rm SNR}_{\rm diff}\simeq4.6$ for the network, where the effect becomes measurable and displaces the spectral cutoff by half of the statistical error.

papers.title: Self-Force and Bremsstrahlung in Finite Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study the self-force and the accompanying Bremsstrahlung for a moving point charge in nonlinear electrodynamics with finite self-field and self-energy. The self-force in the Maxwell theory has been the subject of many studies, often by renowned physicists. After reviewing Coleman's lucid treatise for Maxwell among them, we wish to explore the same question in the Born--Infeld theory, our prototype. We independently compute the local self-force and the global radiative dissipation, and show how the two are mutually consistent. Despite the nonlinearity turning off for the asymptotic radiative field, its residual effect survives via the effective multipole moments of a moving charge, allowing deviation from Maxwell. We close with a detailed discussion about two different manifestations of the self-force in the literature and how these enter our computation. One of the appendices explores Born--Infeld ModMax as a generalization.

papers.title: Toward the minimal set of states in axion superradiance
papers.abstract: Observational searches for black hole superradiance require predicting the growth and evolution of quasi-bound states on astrophysical timescales. For axions (and most light spin-0 particles), self-interactions efficiently redistribute energy and angular momentum from the fastest-growing superradiant states into higher-order, more weakly bound states, and do so on short timescales. This has made it difficult to compute even the most mundane of observables across large regions of parameter space. In this work we extend the study of self-interacting systems, following the evolution of nearly 300 coupled quasi-bound states. We evolve a $10\,M_\odot$ black hole over a Salpeter timescale, and $10^4$ and $10^8\,M_\odot$ black holes over a Gyr, identifying for each axion mass the minimal set of states required to describe the evolution of the black hole and the shape of the superradiant cloud. In most cases the evolution converges as increasingly weakly bound states are added; we identify no less than 203 distinct quasi-bound states that play a role in establishing this convergence. In small regions of parameter space, however, we find no converged solution, and show that broad resonant features and nearly degenerate scattering rates redistribute mass to bound states with principal quantum numbers $n \gtrsim 45$. We further show that the cloud can extend to radii orders of magnitude larger than usually assumed, that gravitational-wave level transitions can prevent the growth of superradiant states, and that both the gravitational-wave spectrum and the interaction with the environment are far richer than previously appreciated.

papers.title: Improved delensing of CMB $B$-modes with upcoming SO and LSST Year-1 mock dataset: Impact of photometric redshift errors
papers.abstract: In the era of high-precision Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) anisotropy measurements, detection of primordial gravitational waves (PGWs) is one of the main goals of current CMB experiments. Detection of a divergence-free ($B$-mode) component in CMB polarisation will provide direct evidence of inflationary PGWs in the early universe. However, weak gravitational lensing of CMB photons due to intervening mass distribution of the Universe distorts the primordial polarisation patterns, introducing an additional lensing-induced $B$-mode signal. Removing these lensing-induced $B$-modes is essential for improving constraints on the amplitude of PGWs. In this work, we present a multi-tracer delensing analysis using simulations of the Rubin Observatory LSST galaxy catalogue and Simons Observatory (SO) CMB maps. We use realistic photometric redshift errors for LSST mock catalogue and high complexity Galactic foregrounds for CMB simulations. By adopting a tomographic multi-tracer approach that combines the CMB and LSST mock data, we achieved a 10-20% higher delensing efficiency compared with using CMB data alone. Our analysis removes approximately 60% of the lensing-induced $B$-mode power. We find that photometric redshift errors in the mock galaxy catalogue introduce biases in the inferred galaxy bias and $σ_{8,0}$ parameters. However, these uncertainties do not produce a significant systematic bias in the inferred tensor-to-scalar ratio.

papers.title: Search for gravitational wave coincident neutrinos in DEAP-3600
papers.abstract: We searched DEAP-3600 data for neutrino signals coincident with gravitational waves from compact object mergers observed by the LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA collaborations (LVK). While mergers involving neutron stars are expected to produce neutrinos, these have never been detected. The DEAP-3600 experiment is sensitive to electron neutrinos as recently observed through charged current neutrino absorption on its $^{40}$Ar target. Between 2016 and 2020, the detector recorded data during seven compact merger events involving neutron stars that were observed gravitationally by LVK. Upon examination, there is no statistically significant evidence of neutrinos from any of the mergers analyzed. Exclusion limits are set on the electron neutrino fluence, e.g. from GW170817 in the mono-energetic model at $6.8\times10^{12}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$ ($1.8\times10^{10}~\text{cm$^{-2}$}$) for 10 MeV (100 MeV) neutrinos.

papers.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
papers.abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.

papers.title: Strong Lensing Tomography: Double and pseudo multi-source plane strong gravitational lensing to constrain dark energy
papers.abstract: Tomographic measurements of gravitational lensing with different lens and source redshift distributions contain crucial information about the universe's relative expansion rate, and hence dark energy. While this technique is well-established in weak lensing, its application to strong lensing has traditionally focused on Double Source Plane Lenses (DSPLs). However, DSPLs are exceedingly rare and fundamentally limited by the Mass-Sheet Degeneracy (MSD), a systematic uncertainty underexplored in previous literature.
