This stands in contrast to a previous study that relied on a classical nucleation framework. By performing radiative transfer simulations that incorporate dust formation, we demonstrate that, if formed, r-process dust could naturally explain the observed late-time infrared emission, although refining ejecta parameters and geometry will be necessary to match specific observational cases. The formation and abundance of r-process dust are highly sensitive to ejecta mass, composition, and expansion velocity. Infrared emission from r-process dust may therefore potentially serve a new probe of heavy-element production in neutron star mergers.

papers.title: ACORN I. Massive Black Hole Seeding and Tidal Disruption Events from Star Clusters in Cosmological Simulations
papers.abstract: JWST has revealed massive star clusters at $z\gtrsim 6$, which provide promising environments for massive black hole (MBH) seed formation. We introduce a new MBH seeding model for cosmological simulations, physically motivated by runaway collisions in star clusters. Subgrid star clusters are generated according to the local ISM and evolved through stellar evolution and two-body relaxation. The masses of MBH seeds formed through runaway collisions are determined by the properties of their host clusters, including the effects of metallicity-dependent stellar winds. We further follow tidal disruption events (TDEs) with the evolving clusters, which can be enhanced in MBH binaries, and account for gravitational-wave (GW) recoil following MBH mergers. We implement this model in a constrained simulation of a 5$σ$ overdense region, where seeds of $10^{3}-10^{5.6}\,M_\odot$ form in clusters with $10^{4}\leq m_{\rm SC}\leq 10^{8}\,M_\odot$. Because both the seed abundance and mass are directly connected to the local environment, we have a more physical $M_{\rm BH}\!-\!M_{\rm galaxy}$ scaling for low-mass galaxies ($M_{\rm galaxy}\sim10^{6-9}\,M_\odot$), a regime poorly described by previous seeding models. Multiple MBHs are naturally allowed to form in-situ within individual halos, producing a spatially clustered population. This increases the MBH merger rate by $\sim100$ relative to other seeding models, significantly enhancing the expected LISA event rate. TDEs can dominate the growth of $10^{3-4}\,M_\odot$ MBHs and produce luminous flares of $L_{\rm peak}\sim 10^{42-43}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$, increasing the observability of low-mass seeds. This seeding prescription accelerates early MBH growth at $z\gtrsim 8$, while subsequent self-regulated gas accretion drives the central MBH toward similar masses $\sim10^{9}\, M_\odot$ by $z=6$ across different seeding models.

papers.title: Self-interacting dark matter and neutrino masses from MeV-scale lepton-number breaking
papers.abstract: We show that a scalar whose vacuum expectation value (vev) breaks lepton number at the MeV scale, generating the light-neutrino masses through the inverse seesaw, can also serve as the light mediator of self-interacting dark matter. Dark matter is a pseudo-Dirac fermion whose mass splitting arises from the same vev and is predicted to be proportional to the self-interaction coupling times the vev. A strong central interaction between the dark states requires this splitting to be sizable. The CP-even mediator decays into neutrinos at a rate fixed by the neutrino masses, independent of its mixing with the Higgs boson. Fixing the coupling by the relic abundance and evaluating exact partial-wave cross sections, the model reproduces the velocity dependence of the self-interaction cross section inferred from dwarf galaxies to clusters along a narrow band, $m_s\simeq1.9~{\rm MeV}\times(m_χ/{\rm GeV})$, extending up to $m_χ\simeq12$~GeV with a best fit at $m_χ\simeq7.6$~GeV and $m_s\simeq15$~MeV, and on a sequence of resonant islands of comparable fit quality at higher masses. The cluster data bound the dark matter mass from above, so that the allowed masses extend from about $3$ to $70$~GeV ($95\%$ confidence level), with correlated mediator masses of $6$-$28$~MeV. Combining constraints from the effective number of neutrino species, SN~1987A and direct detection, we find the lepton-number-breaking scale confined to a window of a few hundred MeV and a strong preference for normal neutrino mass ordering. The allowed parameter space is testable by future measurements of $N_{\rm eff}$, low-threshold direct detection and the neutrino mass ordering.

papers.title: Quasinormal overtones and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar quasinormal modes (QNMs), with particular attention to overtones, and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes, which interpolate between the Reissner--Nordström (RN) and Hayward limits. Over the allowed ranges of charge $q$ and regularization parameter $α_0$, all QNM frequencies have negative imaginary parts, confirming stability against scalar perturbations. Increasing either $q$ or $α_0$ can trigger overtone outbursts, with the Frolov threshold shifted to smaller parameter values than in the RN or Hayward cases. Angular momentum does not eliminate the outburst but postpones its onset from $n=1$ at $l=0$ to $n\geq 2$ at $l=1$. Comparisons of the effective potential show that, for $l=1$, charge raises the barrier peak much more strongly than $α_0$, while the clearest deviations from the Hayward and RN references are localized near the horizon. Using the QNM--grey-body correspondence at $l=1$, we find that overtone corrections are essential, and the amended formula substantially outperforms the eikonal truncation. At fixed frequency, both $q$ and $α_0$ suppress transmission, with charge being the dominant factor, consistent with the stronger barrier enhancement under the charge scan.

papers.title: Low-mass failed supernovae and the $10\,M_{\odot}$ peak in the merging black hole mass distribution
papers.abstract: Gravitational-wave observations reveal that the rate of merging black holes drops by $\sim2$ orders of magnitude from component masses $\sim 10\,M_{\odot}$ to $\sim 15\,M_{\odot}$. The increased compactness of the black hole progenitor cores may contribute to the $\sim 10\,M_{\odot}$ overdensity, but cannot fully explain the rate difference. In this paper, we consider the possibility that the overdensity is reinforced by supernova processes that result in efficient black hole formation from direct collapse in a narrow range around $10\, M_{\odot}$. We extend previous studies by considering a distinct subpopulation of failed-supernovae black holes, possibly separated by a gap in the primary mass distribution from the rest of the population. Using 153 observations from the latest GWTC-4.0 catalog, we confirm a strong peak in the primary mass distribution at $10\,M_{\odot}$, with a peak rate density of $7.36_{-3.11}^{+6.35}$ $M_{\odot}^{-1}\mathrm{yr}^{-1} \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}$. The rate drops sharply and becomes consistent with zero at the 90 % level for primary mass $m_1\in (12.0, 16.1)\, M_{\odot}$, then rises again to confidently nonzero values above $\sim 16\,M_{\odot}$ before falling at higher masses. Our results reveal structure in the mass distribution in the $10-20\,M_{\odot}$ range, with rate changes of multiple orders of magnitude across a few solar masses, consistent with a distinct population of failed-supernova black holes. These conclusions persist in the latest GWTC-5.0 catalog.

papers.title: Expiscating the black hole singularity in holography
papers.abstract: We argue that the leading exponential rate in the high frequency asymptotics of holographic thermal two-point functions is independent of the conformal dimension and spin (held fixed) of the operator. We analyze the leading universal WKB spectral curve governing the asymptotics at non-vanishing momentum scaling with frequency. We show that its classical action governs time domain signatures of the bouncing geodesic singularity, highly damped quasinormal modes, and the asymptotics of multi-stress tensor OPE coefficients. Beyond the leading order, we examine linear and dimension-dependent sublinear scalings of momentum with frequency. In both regimes, we derive the connection matrix between the boundary and the horizon using exact-WKB techniques. The results show a factorization of the spectral function into a perturbative part controlled by the OPE and a non-perturbative part governed by WKB transport. For linear scaling at fixed $k/ω$ in the timelike regime, the turning points controlling physical transport remain separated from the curvature singularity. Nevertheless, a singularity-anchored representative of the same transport homology class determines the leading WKB action. In the sublinear regime, the relevant turning points approach the singularity. We match an exact solution of the near-singularity scaled equation to the exterior WKB solution to determine the connection matrix and spectral function. Our results clarify how the black hole curvature singularity is encoded in dual field theory observables at leading order in the planar expansion.

papers.title: Magnetic field-induced enhancement and quenching of Urca emission in quark matter
papers.abstract: Using first-principles field-theoretic methods, we investigate neutrino emission from strongly magnetized dense quark matter under conditions relevant to compact stars. We account for Landau-level quantization of both electron and quark states and show that it strongly modifies the kinematics of Urca processes. In particular, quark quantization restricts the available phase space in which both quark and electron energies can simultaneously lie near their respective Fermi surfaces. At moderately strong magnetic fields, before pronounced quark quantization sets in, the emission rate tends to increase on average with increasing field strength. In the regime of very strong fields, however, the increasingly restricted phase space first gives rise to Shubnikov--de Haas-type oscillations and then to resonance-like spikes near a discrete sequence of Urca-resonant magnetic field values, separated by regions of strong suppression. Finally, the emission rate becomes nearly completely quenched once $|eB| \gtrsim 6μ_{e}μ_{u}$, corresponding to approximately $B\gtrsim 1.5\times 10^{19}~\mbox{G}$ for the representative set of model parameters considered. We also find significant anisotropy in the longitudinal momentum emission near the Urca-resonant magnetic field values.

papers.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
papers.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

papers.title: Density-induced dark-baryon conversion in $Δ-$admixed hypernuclear neutron stars
papers.abstract: We investigate density-induced conversion of neutrons into a neutral dark baryon $χ$ in cold, charge-neutral, $β$-equilibrated neutron-star matter containing hyperons and all $Δ(1232)$ quartet. The hadronic sector is modeled within a density-dependent covariant density-functional framework using the DDME2 parametrization. A scalar Higgs portal is included as a possible interaction channel between the visible and dark sectors, although its mean-field contribution is negligible for the couplings adopted here. Unlike fixed dark-matter admixture models or scenarios in which nucleon-to-DM conversion is driven by Higgs exchange, the $χ$ abundance is determined self-consistently from chemical equilibrium and baryon-number conservation. We find that hyperons and $Δ$ resonances alter the neutron chemical potential, delay the onset of $χ$, and suppress its abundance relative to nucleonic matter. This competition induces characteristic changes in the equation of state, particle fractions, sound speed, and adiabatic index. For $m_χ=1250$, $1300$, and $1400$ MeV, the maximum masses of the complete $N+Y+Δ+χ$ configurations are $1.806$, $1.899$ and $2.024,M_\odot$, respectively, indicating that the massive-pulsar constraint disfavors the lighter dark-baryon benchmarks. The radial profiles further show that for $m_χ=1400$ MeV, $χ$ is confined to the inner core of the most massive stars, while canonical configurations remain essentially unaffected. Thus, the stellar modifications arise primarily from conversion-induced rearrangement of the equilibrium composition rather than from Higgs-mediated interactions. These results highlight the importance of treating conventional non-nucleonic degrees of freedom and density-generated dark baryons on an equal footing when assessing the astrophysical viability of dark-sector extensions of dense matter.

papers.title: Living on the Edge of Effective Field Theory: Near-Extremal Black Holes in Quadratic Gravity
papers.abstract: Near-extremal black holes can amplify higher-derivative corrections to general relativity, making them sharp probes of the perturbative control of gravitational effective field theory. We study this question in quadratic gravity with a dynamical scalar degree of freedom, focusing on dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Using pseudospectral methods, we construct rapidly rotating exterior solutions at fixed surface gravity and fixed horizon angular velocity, and follow this controlled family toward extremality. In dynamical Chern-Simons gravity, the sequence approaches an asymptotically flat extremal exterior whose near-horizon limit agrees with the dynamical-Chern-Simons-deformed near-horizon extremal Kerr geometry and inherits its enhanced $SO(2,1)\times U(1)$ symmetry. In scalar Gauss-Bonnet gravity, the same limiting procedure behaves differently: the scalar develops an unavoidable logarithmic singularity at the horizon, the exterior metric develops a small boundary layer near the horizon, and the scalar-Gauss-Bonnet-deformed near-horizon extremal solution is not connected to a regular asymptotically flat exterior. We then use curvature invariants and tidal forces to diagnose the breakdown of the perturbative effective-field-theory expansion. We find that scalar curvature invariants can remain finite at the horizon even when tidal forces measured by infalling observers diverge as inverse powers of the surface gravity. These results separate distinct notions of effective-field-theory breakdown near extremality and provide a perturbative validity estimate that can be compared with current bounds on the dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar-Gauss-Bonnet couplings.

papers.title: Discovery of a Short-Duration Fast X-ray Transient Associated with a Short Gamma-Ray Burst
papers.abstract: Extragalactic fast X-ray transients (EFXTs) are an emerging population of high-energy transients with diverse physical origins. Only a few observed EFXTs are associated with compact object mergers, and the known events generally display X-ray emission lasting much longer than their associated short gamma-ray bursts (GRBs). Here we report EP260411a, an $\sim8$-s EFXT discovered in archival Einstein Probe Wide-field X-ray Telescope (EP-WXT) observations through a time-targeted search for X-ray counterparts of short GRBs. This fast X-ray transient is temporally coincident with short GRB 260411A, with both the pulse width and peak time showing clear anticorrelations with the characteristic photon energy across the gamma-ray and soft X-ray bands. Joint EP-WXT and Fermi-GBM spectral fitting further shows that the broadband emission can be described by a cutoff power-law model with an additional low-energy spectral break, suggesting a common origin for the single-pulse X-ray and gamma-ray emission. The resulting properties place the event within the Type I GRB region in the $E_{\rm p,z}$-$E_{\rm iso}$ plane, supporting its classification as a compact object merger event. Unlike previously known merger-driven Type I EFXTs with long-lasting X-ray emission, EP260411a reveals that the Type I EFXT population can also extend to the short timescale of a few seconds. papers.title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
papers.abstract: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. A single object then has a minimum classical-gravity noise (CGN), S_F^min = 2 hbar M Omega_SN^2, where Omega_SN is the Schrodinger-Newton frequency set by the microscopic mass distribution. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

papers.title: Searching for Massive Scalar Fields with non-minimal Curvature Couplings in LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Ringdown Signals
papers.abstract: We search for massive scalar fields with non-minimal curvature couplings using the loudest ringdown signals observed by LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA. We find that current ringdown observations do not provide informative constraints on the scalar-field mass. We nevertheless constrain the coupling length scale for scalar fields satisfying $Mμ<1$, where $μ$ is the scalar-field mass, yielding marginalized 90$\%$ credible upper limits of 60.4 km and 59.8 km for dynamical Chern-Simons and scalar Gauss-Bonnet couplings, respectively.

papers.title: Einstein Reconstruction Scheme: Metric Reconstruction by Direct Inversion of the Einstein Operator
papers.abstract: We propose a metric reconstruction scheme that computes the metric directly from the linearized Einstein equations for noncompact sources. Working in a traceful radiation gauge, we hierarchically solve four Einstein transport equations, with the remaining six enforced by suitable homogeneous data. Unlike previous Newman-Penrose approaches, we show how the homogeneous data are fixed, thereby closing the full set of Einstein equations. We conclude by relating our scheme to existing sourced reconstruction methods, thus establishing a connection between the Newman-Penrose and Hertz-potential approaches.

papers.title: Radiative stability of species-separated Kaluza--Klein spectra in warped geometry
papers.abstract: Species-dependent fifth-direction lightcones, generated by scalar-gradient operators, can separate gauge and fermion Kaluza--Klein (KK) scales in a warped extra dimension, as recently shown by Randall and Riojas. In this work, we study whether this separation survives quantum corrections. Quark loops can only move the gluon speed within the interval spanned by the bare speeds. Gluon exchange pulls the quark speed toward the gluon speed, with a one-loop coefficient strongly enhanced by fifth-component exchange when the gluon is the slow species. We set the size of this effect using the strong-coupling estimates for a light-gluon benchmark, where a $5.5$~TeV gluon sits below quark partners at $10.74$~TeV. Within the effective theory, the Kaluza--Klein (KK) modes then correct the quark speed at order one. That correction is several times larger than the mass ordering can absorb, so the light-gluon ordering has no perturbative protection. The reverse benchmark, with slow quarks and a heavy gluon, keeps its ordering roughly ten times more robust.
